facts.text: The only major-college team of the 1950s to lose every game (15+ games): The Citadel, 1954-55 — 0-17.
Only two major-college teams of the 1950s averaged 95 points a game (15+ games): Morehead St. (1955-56: 95.9 ppg, 19-10); Furman (1954-55: 95.3 ppg, 17-10).

Just four major-college players of the 1950s attempted 800 field goals: Frank Selvy (1953-54: 427-941 FG); Darrell Floyd (1955-56: 339-850 FG); Rod Hundley (1955-56: 290-814 FG); Grady Wallace (1956-57: 336-803 FG).
Just three major-college players of the 1950s averaged 35 points a game (15+ games): Frank Selvy (1953-54: 41.7 ppg); Darrell Floyd (1954-55: 35.9 ppg); Oscar Robertson (1957-58: 35.1 ppg).
Just three major-college teams of the 1950s went unbeaten (20+ games): UNC (1956-57: 32-0); San Francisco (1955-56: 29-0); Kentucky (1953-54: 25-0).
Just three major-college teams of the 1950s lost just once (20+ games): San Francisco (1954-55: 28-1); Miss. St. (1958-59: 24-1); Columbia (1950-51: 21-1).
Most 700-point seasons in the 1950s: Oscar Robertson, 3 (1957-58, 1958-59, 1959-60).
Most 90-point-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 1950s: Furman, 3 (1952-53, 1953-54, 1954-55).
7 major-college players scored 900 points in the 1950s (11 seasons). The most extreme: Frank Selvy, 1953-54 — 1,209 pts in 29 games.
5 major-college players made 300 free throws in the 1950s (6 seasons). The most extreme: Johnny O'Brien, 1951-52 — 361-475 FT.
13 major-college players attempted 350 free throws in the 1950s (16 seasons). The most extreme: Johnny O'Brien, 1951-52 — 361-475 FT.
16 major-college players grabbed 500 rebounds in the 1950s (18 seasons). The most extreme: Leroy Wright, 1958-59 — 652 rebounds.
Most 700-point seasons by one school's players in the 1950s: West Virginia, 5 (Jerry West, Rod Hundley, Mark Workman).
Highest rebounding average in a season in the 1950s: Maurice Stokes, Saint Francis (PA), 1953-54 — 26.5 rpg.
Most free throws made in a season in the 1950s: Johnny O'Brien, Seattle, 1951-52 — 361.
Best field-goal percentage in a season (200+ attempts) in the 1950s: Joe Holup, George Washington, 1955-56 — 0.647%.
Best free-throw percentage in a season (100+ attempts) in the 1950s: James Scott, West Texas State, 1954-55 — 0.895%.
Highest team scoring average in a season in the 1950s: Morehead St., 1955-56 — 95.9 ppg (19-10).
Most losses in a season in the 1950s: Washington St., 1952-53 — 7-27.
Best team field-goal percentage in a season in the 1950s: Auburn, 1959-60 — 0.521%.
Highest scoring average in a season in the 1950s: Frank Selvy, Furman, 1953-54 — 41.7 ppg.
Most points in a season in the 1950s: Frank Selvy, Furman, 1953-54 — 1,209.
Most points of the 1950s: Oscar Robertson, 2,973.
Most rebounds of the 1950s: Tom Gola, 2,201.
Most free throws made in the 1950s: Dickie Hemric, 905.
11 major-college players averaged 30 points a game (15+ games) in the 1950s (15 seasons). The most extreme: Frank Selvy, 1953-54 — 41.7 ppg.
21 major-college players averaged 25 points and 15 rebounds (15+ games) in the 1950s (26 seasons). The most extreme: Oscar Robertson, 1957-58 — 35.1 ppg, 15.2 rpg.
5 major-college teams won 30 games in the 1950s. The most extreme: UNC, 1956-57 — 32-0.
13 major-college teams lost 22 games in the 1950s (14 seasons). The most extreme: Washington St., 1952-53 — 7-27.
29 major-college players averaged 20 rebounds a game (15+ games) in the 1950s (38 seasons). The most extreme: Maurice Stokes, 1953-54 — 26.5 rpg.
9 major-college players averaged 22 rebounds a game (15+ games) in the 1950s (14 seasons). The most extreme: Maurice Stokes, 1953-54 — 26.5 rpg.

method: College basketball (men's): each line is one Stathead (Sports Reference college basketball) Season Finder query over the decade's ten seasons (a decade is the seasons starting in its years: the 1970s run 1970-71 to 1979-80), run in a signed-in subscriber session; result rows and stable ids are stored as provenance.

Sports Reference's season finders begin with 1947-48, so the 1940s page covers two seasons and earlier decades are not in the record. Rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and the three-pointer (1986-87) arrive at different times; rules on a stat a season lacks return nothing. Per-game figures are totals divided by games.
